description:
Redwood Inference is standing up a reliable, repeatable sales demo environment (“demo tenant”) paired with a scripted talk track and a standard deck. The goal is to make every AE/SE-run demo consistent, fast to set up, and resilient to common failure modes (quota issues, model rollout changes, capacity constraints, auth misconfig, dashboard emptiness). The scope spans (1) a production-like demo tenant with “known-good” scenarios (hosted API + Dedicated-style controls + Private/VPC talking points), (2) automation to provision/reset the tenant and seed realistic data (projects, API keys, usage, dashboards, prompt sets/evals), and (3) sales enablement artifacts (deck, talk track, objection handling, competitive framing, security FAQ links, and demo certification).

Key scenarios to be supported end-to-end:
- Core API demo: chat completions w/ streaming, structured output, tool calling, retries.
- “Production economics” demo: batching/caching toggles, latency vs cost tradeoffs, token-level breakdowns.
- Reliability demo: fallback routing to compatible model variants/regions; graceful degradation story.
- Observability demo: Console dashboards, traces, error analysis, rollout view (canary/A-B) with a safe synthetic workload.
- Enterprise/security demo (mostly narrative + screenshots): SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, retention controls, VPC/Private deployment architecture.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Go-to-market: Stephanie Nguyen / Lukas Meyer (sales leadership), Avery Johnson / Priyom Das / Hannah Schmitt (AEs), Markus Klein + SE team (delivery + technical demo ownership).
- Marketing/product marketing: Soojin Lee + Camila Reyes (messaging, deck, competitive).
- DevEx: Alex Martinez + Monica Patel + Renee Sullivan (SDK/examples/docs support for demo scripts).
- Engineering/SRE: Ethan Park (control plane/config), Sean Gallagher (reliability/SLOs), plus Eng Platform for Console/demo-data seeding.
- Security & Compliance consult: ensure demo data is synthetic and access controls are correct.

Phases and timeline (typical 6–8 weeks):
1) Requirements + narrative (week 1): define personas, ICP-specific variants (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and success criteria; align on “demo happy path” and “objection paths”.
2) Demo tenant build (weeks 2–4): environment isolation, provisioning, seeded datasets, stable model/version pins, synthetic traffic generator, and reset automation; add runbooks.
3) Talk track + deck (weeks 3–5): story arc, slide content, live steps, backup screenshots, timing, handoffs between AE/SE.
4) Internal enablement (weeks 5–6): training sessions, certification checklist, feedback loop; update enablement docs.
5) Maintenance (ongoing): monitoring, alerts, monthly refresh of scenarios/models, and incident process for demo outages.

Constraints:
- Must avoid customer data; all metrics/logs should be synthetic.
- Must remain stable across model catalog changes; pin versions and define a controlled rollout path.
- Must be fast to reset between demos (minutes, not hours) and support parallel demos.
- Must be secure: least-privilege keys, short-lived credentials, audited access, and clear sharing rules.

files.description: Canonical sales demo deck outline: slide-by-slide narrative (problem, why now, Redwood differentiators, live demo sections, ROI framing), plus appendix for enterprise/security and deployment modes.
Scripted talk track tied to the deck: exact phrasing for transitions, questions to ask, optional branches (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and timing guidance.
Defined demo personas (ML platform lead, app engineer, security reviewer, procurement) and the mapped ‘known-good’ scenarios each persona cares about.
One-pager for common competitor comparisons and objection handling (latency claims, pricing misconceptions, build-vs-buy, private deployment concerns).
Curated security FAQ for demos: short answers + links to deeper internal references (SOC2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, encryption/KMS, retention/residency).
Guidance for demo-friendly pricing talk: how to discuss usage-based pricing, Dedicated commits, POC credits, and guardrails for discounting/escalations.
Operational runbook: how to reset demo tenant state, re-seed scenarios, rotate keys, verify dashboards, and validate model pins; includes expected timings and verification checklist.
How-to: architecture of the demo environment (accounts, projects, orgs), dependency map (control plane, console, billing sandbox), and ownership boundaries between Eng and GTM.
SLO/SLA targets specifically for demo environment (availability, latency percentiles, dashboard freshness), plus error-budget policy and escalation path.
Capacity guidance for parallel demos: reserved GPU pool sizing assumptions, quota configuration, rate limits, and how to respond to capacity-related demo failures.
PRD for the demo tenant: user stories (AE/SE), required scenarios, non-functional requirements, ‘backup mode’ requirements (screenshots/recordings), and success metrics.
ADR documenting the approach to pinning models/versions for demos, allowed fallbacks, and how to keep the demo stable while still reflecting the real product.
Working notes from kickoff: goals, scope, open questions, stakeholders, and an initial list of ‘known-good’ demo scenarios.
Iterative draft of the spoken talk track with inline timing marks, optional branches by customer type, and placeholders for screenshots.
Slide outline with speaker notes and TODOs; includes alternative slide orders for PLG-to-enterprise vs enterprise-first narratives.
Checklist used by SEs before each demo: verify tenant health, seed data present, keys valid, dashboards show traffic, and fallback behavior tested.
Internal FAQ for reps: common questions during demos (pricing, security, latency) with draft answers and escalation contacts.
Enablement plan: training session agenda, certification rubric, pass/fail criteria, and a feedback form template.
Brainstorm doc listing likely demo failures (quota, auth, model change, dashboard empty) and prepared backup paths (recording, screenshots, canned outputs).
Question bank aligned to the talk track: qualification prompts and decision-maker probing to tailor the demo live.
Sheet-like doc: how to track demo usage (number of demos, scenario completion, time to reset, demo failure rate) and owners for reporting.
Draft policy for who gets access to demo tenant, how keys are shared, rotation cadence, and rules for recording/screensharing.
Compilation of proof points and benchmark snippets appropriate for demo narration; notes on which are safe to share externally.
Run-of-show doc for a standard 30-minute demo: minute-by-minute plan, handoff cues (AE↔SE), and the exact live steps to execute.
Working spec for seeded org/projects/models/routes/prompt sets, including naming conventions and how to ensure dashboards look realistic.
Lightweight QA bug tracker (Drive doc) capturing issues found during dry runs, severity, and links to Linear/GitHub items.
Prep notes for enterprise security reviewers: which artifacts to show, which to avoid, and how to answer ‘data retention/residency’ clearly.
PM ticket to drive scope agreement for the demo environment: acceptance criteria, must-have scenarios, and timeline milestones.
Define and freeze the ‘known-good’ scenario set, expected outputs, and what constitutes a demo regression.
Engineering work item for automation to provision/reset demo tenant (scripts, APIs, idempotency), with sub-tasks and rollout plan.
Generate synthetic traffic and seed events so Console dashboards (cost/latency/errors) populate reliably during demos.
Implement model pinning and a safe fallback policy for demo routes; include monitoring for model catalog changes.
Key management improvements for demo environment: scoped keys, rotation workflow, and auditability.
Create a one-command reset + health check for SEs (CLI or internal tool), with clear pass/fail signals.
Add metrics/alerts specific to demo environment (dashboard freshness, error rate spikes, capacity) and a Slack alert route.
Design task to produce annotated screenshots for backup mode and to standardize the console tour (where to click, what to point out).
